findings_qualitative.value: The radial gradient of r21 in the disk is bimodal: SA galaxies (plus NGC 3627 and NGC 4321) have a constant or shallow gradient out to 0.4 R25, whereas SB galaxies (plus NGC 4536 and NGC 4579) decrease by ~20% before 0.4 R25 (corresponding to the stellar bar radius) and flatten beyond.

evidence.quote: We find, however, that the radial gradient in r 21 is bimodal, where a group containing all SA galaxies prefer constant or very shallow r 21 gradients out to 40% of the optical radius, while another group containing all SB galaxies have a steep r 21 gradient, decreasing by ∼20% before 40% of the optical radius, which also corresponds to the radius of the stellar bar.

All SA galaxies and two in the SAB classification (i.e., NGC 3627 and NGC 4321) maintain a constant or very shallow gradient in r 21 out to 0.4R 25, decreasing only by ∼ 5%. On the other hand, all SB galaxies and the remaining SABs (i.e., NGC 4536 and NGC 4579) quickly decrease in r 21 by 15% already before 0.3R 25, reaching 20% before 0.4R 25 .

claims.finding: r21 is systematically higher in kinematic outliers than in the rotating galactic disk regardless of galaxy morphology.

evidence.quote: The normalized distribution matches the non-normalized distribution very well, and a Welch's t-test between the disk and outliers in the normalized data set gives a p-value of 0.009, indicating that the disk and outliers likely come from different distributions.
The outliers have a statistically larger mean value of r 21 = 0.69 ± 0.10 compared to the disk with r 21 = 0.62 ± 0.08.

claims.hypothesis: The galaxy-averaged r21 depends on galaxy bar morphology (SA, SAB, SB).
claims.experiment: Compare the mean, standard deviation, and normalized PV-pixel number distributions of r21 among SA, SAB, and SB galaxies using Welch's t-test.
claims.result: Mean disk r21 is 0.64 +/- 0.06 (SA), 0.61 +/- 0.08 (SAB), and 0.60 +/- 0.10 (SB), and Welch's t-tests show no significant differences.
claims.finding: There is no significant difference in the average r21 between galaxies with and without bars at TP resolution.

evidence.quote: We compare r 21 between SA, SAB, and SB galaxies, and find no significant difference in the average r 21 depending on the presence of galactic bars.
A Welch's t-test was performed between SA, SAB, and SB galaxies separately for the normalized distribution of disks and outliers, and none indicated any significant differences in the distribution.

claims.hypothesis: Large-scale radial gradients in r21 within the rotating disk vary systematically with galaxy bar morphology.
claims.experiment: Measure radial profiles of r21 in the disk component along the major axis normalized to the central 28" value, optical radius R25, and bar radius RA2.
claims.result: All SA galaxies and two SABs (NGC 3627, NGC 4321) decrease by only ~5% out to 0.4 R25, while all SB galaxies and two SABs (NGC 4536, NGC 4579) decrease by ~20% before 0.4 R25 (~10% at the bar radius RA2) and flatten outside the bar.
claims.finding: The radial gradient of r21 is bimodal, with nonbarred galaxies showing flat/shallow profiles and strongly barred galaxies showing a steep radial decline across the stellar bar region.

evidence.quote: All SA galaxies and two in the SAB classification (i.e., NGC 3627 and NGC 4321) maintain a constant or very shallow gradient in r 21 out to 0.4R 25, decreasing only by ∼ 5%. On the other hand, all SB galaxies and the remaining SABs (i.e., NGC 4536 and NGC 4579) quickly decrease in r 21 by 15% already before 0.3R 25, reaching 20% before 0.4R 25 .
At radii well outside of the bars, even the galaxies with rapidly decreasing r 21 transition to a mode of more stable r 21 with a shallow gradient, much like the SA galaxies.

why_this_data.value: ALMA TP array observations of both CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) provide zero-spacing total fluxes free from interferometric imaging uncertainties and superior flux calibration (~2.4%-5%) compared to conventional single-dish telescopes (20%-30%).

evidence.quote: The calibration precision offered by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) largely surpasses most conventional radio telescopes.
These single dish observations provide zero-spacing information, so are free from uncertainties that can potentially be introduced in the imaging process of interferometer data.

why_this_method.value: Because the ~3 kpc TP spatial resolution smears out spatial structures, high-S/N major-axis PV diagrams and 3DBarolo tilted-ring models are used to spectrally resolve r21 variations and separate noncircular/nuclear kinematic outliers from the rotating disk.

evidence.quote: We exploit the high S/N afforded by ALMA to spectrally resolve the variation in r 21, and investigate its relation to kinematic signatures.

In order to distinguish between the edges of the PV diagrams and the normal galactic rotation in a physically motivated manner, we use 3DBarolo (E. M. Di Teodoro & F. Fraternali 2015) to fit the data cube with a tilted-ring model (D. H. Rogstad et al. 1974).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Modeling galaxy kinematics using CO 21 instead of CO 10 in 3DBarolo, which yielded nearly identical PV diagrams and consistent results, though CO 10 was preferred for its lower critical density and wider mapped area.

evidence.quote: We used CO 10 to model the galaxy instead of CO 21 because we can expect its lower critical density to allow us to trace the bulk of gas and also because the area mapped in CO 10 is wider compared to CO 21, thereby giving a better representation of the whole galaxy.

The PV diagrams of both CO lines were nearly identical, and using CO 21 to model the galaxy parameters produced consistent results in the analyses, even though we use the S/N ratio for the distinction of disks and outliers.

how_they_decided_enough.value: A 20 sigma cut (10 sigma for NGC 1512 and NGC 4579) on CO 10 PV diagrams ensures S/N > 10 over most of CO 21 to detect r21 variations <= 0.05; disk/outlier boundary tested by varying model contour threshold by +/- 5 sigma.

evidence.quote: Considering that the typical range of r 21 is 0.4 to 0.8 within and between galaxies, our high noise level cuts enable us to detect small variations in r 21 of  0.05.
In Figure 2 we also show the contour level 5σ above and below the threshold explained above to illustrate how our choice of the sigma threshold affects the results.

limitations_admitted.value: NGC 628 had to be excluded from the PV analysis due to its very small velocity width (~70 km/s).

evidence.quote: We exclude NGC 628 from this paper because the very small velocity width (∼70km/s) of this galaxy severely limited our analyses using position–velocity (PV) diagrams in Section 3.3.

limitations_admitted.value: The coarse spatial resolution of the TP array (56.6" or ~3.1 kpc) smears out smaller-scale variations (such as star-forming regions, bars, and bar ends) and prevents identifying the exact physical mechanism causing the high-r21 PV outliers.

evidence.quote: It should be noted that the variations we find in this study using the TP array are the minimal variations within the galaxy; larger variations at smaller spatial scales (e.g., with individual star-forming regions) are smeared out.

evidence.loc: 3.5. Physical Origin of High r 21 at Edges of the PV Diagram
evidence.quote: The spatial resolution of our TP array does not allow for detailed investigation on what process is responsible for the elevated r 21 at the edges of our PV diagram, and these will be treated in forthcoming papers using high spatial resolution data sets.
This is likely because we lack the angular resolution to allow us to distinguish the rapid change in r 21 expected from the center, bar, and bar ends.

limitations_admitted.value: The S/N contour thresholds used to separate disk and outlier components in the PV diagram are somewhat arbitrary, and for NGC 3521 and NGC 4579 the outlier separation is sensitive to the threshold choice.

evidence.quote: The S/N cuts used above are somewhat arbitrary.

For NGC 4579, changing the threshold to a lower value (5σ instead of 10σ) results in the whole PV diagram being defined as a disk; the increase in r 21 at the edges of the PV diagram is not prominent in this galaxy, and should be interpreted with care.

limitations_admitted.value: Adjacent radial bins (5.6" width) are not completely independent because they are 1/10 of the 56.6" beam size.

evidence.quote: The width of the radial bins is 5.6 , corresponding to the pixel size, i.e., 1/10 of the beam. Thus, the adjacent radial bins are not completely independent.

referee_caveats_inferred: Differential beam dilution within the 56.6" (~3.1 kpc) TP beam can artificially produce or alter radial gradients and PV-edge ratios if the intrinsic spatial/velocity distributions of CO(2-1) and CO(1-0) differ on sub-kpc scales (e.g., compact nuclear rings vs. extended disks).

The PV analysis is restricted to a 1'-wide slit along the kinematic major axis; for galaxies where the stellar bar is misaligned with the major axis, the major-axis radial profile does not uniformly sample the bar.
Reclassifying NGC 3521 from SABbc to SA reduces the nonbarred SA sample to 4 galaxies and SB to 3 galaxies, making the morphological bimodality rest on a small sample size (11 galaxies total).
